title: 09. Storage, CDN & Data Engineering: CDN & Content Delivery
summary: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) is a geographically distributed network of servers that delivers content to users from the server nearest to them. Reduces latency, offloads origin server, and handles traffic spikes.

sections.title: Detailed Explanation
sections.body:
### What is a CDN?

A **Content Delivery Network (CDN)** is a geographically distributed network of servers that delivers content to users from the server nearest to them. Reduces latency, offloads origin server, and handles traffic spikes.

### How CDNs Work

1. User requests a resource (image, CSS, JS, video)
2. DNS routes to nearest CDN edge server (Point of Presence — PoP)
3. If cached (HIT) → return immediately
4. If not cached (MISS) → fetch from origin, cache at edge, return to user

### Push vs Pull CDN

| Feature  | Push CDN                     | Pull CDN                        |
| -------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Upload   | You push content to CDN      | CDN pulls on first request      |
| Control  | Full control over content    | CDN manages caching             |
| Best for | Static assets, known content | Dynamic content, large catalogs |
| Examples | S3 + CloudFront              | Cloudflare, Akamai              |

### Cache Invalidation Strategies

| Strategy               | Description                       | Pros           | Cons                |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------- |
| TTL (Time-To-Live)     | Cache expires after N seconds     | Simple         | Stale data possible |
| Purge                  | Manually invalidate specific URLs | Precise        | Complex to manage   |
| Versioning             | `/style.v2.css`                   | Instant update | URL changes needed  |
| Stale-while-revalidate | Serve stale, update in background | Fast UX        | Brief staleness     |

diagrams.title: A CDN request: edge hit vs miss
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User in Mumbai
  participant E as Edge PoP (Mumbai)
  participant O as Origin (us-east-1)
  U->>E: GET /video/intro.mp4
  alt cache hit
    E-->>U: 200 from edge (~20 ms)
  else cache miss
    E->>O: fetch object
    O-->>E: 200 + Cache-Control max-age=86400
    E-->>U: 200 (~250 ms, cached for next users)
  end
diagrams.explain: A CDN keeps copies of content in points of presence near users. A **hit** is served from the nearby edge in milliseconds; a **miss** goes to the origin once and is cached for everyone after. `Cache-Control` headers decide how long; versioned file names (`app.3f9c.js`) make invalidation trivial. CDNs also absorb traffic spikes and DDoS before they reach your servers.

quiz.question: Push CDN vs Pull CDN?
options: User requests cdn.example.com. CDN's authoritative DNS server checks user's resolver IP → determines geographic region → returns IP of nearest edge.
(1) Absorb traffic — CDN has massive bandwidth across many PoPs, (2) Distribute attack — anycast spreads traffic across edges, (3) Rate limiting — edge-level rate…

quiz.explanation: Push: You upload content to CDN proactively. Full control, no cache misses on first request. Good for: predictable, static content.

quiz.question: How do you handle cache invalidation in a CDN?
options: (1) Edge computing (Cloudflare Workers) — run code at edge, (2) Short TTL — cache for seconds, not hours, (3) stale-while-revalidate — serve cached, update async, (4)…
Push: You upload content to CDN proactively. Full control, no cache misses on first request.
When cache expires, many concurrent requests all miss cache and hit origin simultaneously.

quiz.explanation: (1) TTL: Set max-age, content expires automatically. (2) Purge API: Explicitly invalidate URLs. (3) Versioned URLs: /app.v2.js — new URL = guaranteed fresh.

quiz.explanation: Architecture: Upload → S3 (original) → Processing queue → Generate variants (thumbnail, medium, HD) → Store variants → CDN. On-request transformation: URL params define size/format → CDN edge transforms → cache result. Use WebP/AVIF for modern browsers (Accept header).
